t:
(a) 
Except for the amendments made by subsection (a) of the first section of this Act, and except for the amendment made by subsection (b) of this section, the amendments made by this Act shall be effective only during the two-year period which begins on the date of enactment of this Act. Upon the expiration of such period, each provision of law amended by this Act, except section 14(b)(1) of the Federal Reserve Act, is amended to read as it did immediately prior to the enactment of this Act.
 
    (b) 
Upon the expiration of the two-year period which begins on the date of enactment of this Act, section 14(b)(1) of the Federal Reserve Act (12 U.S.C. 355(1)) is further amended by adding at the end thereof the following new sentence: “Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, any bonds, notes, or other obligations which are direct obligations of the United States or which are fully guaranteed by the United States as to principal and interest may be bought and sold without regard to maturities but only in the open market.”

fable.w: This section is a sunset and effective-date provision, plus an amendment to the Federal Reserve Act allowing U.S. obligations to be bought and sold in the open market. The tempting reading is that "open market" transactions involve outside parties, but that is a market transaction, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. It contains no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: the amendments made by this Act shall be effective only during the two-year period which begins on the date of enactment of this Act

opus.w: This section is a sunset and effective-date provision. It also adds a sentence letting the Federal Reserve buy and sell government obligations only in the open market. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to challenge a federal decision. The 'open market' wording describes financial transactions, not participation in decision-making.
opus.s: the amendments made by this Act shall be effective only during the two-year period which begins on the date of enactment of this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The phrase "bought and sold ... in the open market" might look like outside parties (banks, investors) dealing with the Federal Reserve. That fails the definition. Market transactions don't involve outsiders being consulted before a federal decision. The rest of the section only sets when the amendments expire and adds a sentence to the Federal Reserve Act. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Federal Reserve Act to allow certain government bonds to be traded in the open market without maturity restrictions. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The reference to the 'open market' describes where the trading occurs, not a participatory process involving outside entities in the decision-making itself.
qwen_chat.s: “Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, any bonds, notes, or other obligations which are direct obligations of the United States or which are fully guaranteed by the United States as to principal and interest may be bought and sold without regard to maturities but only in the open market.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "open market" implies public participation because the general public can buy and sell bonds. However, the definition of participation requires the government to consult or coordinate with outsiders *before* making a decision. Here, the statute simply removes a restriction on trading; it does not require the government to seek input from the public or any outside entity regarding the decision to allow these trades. The "open market" is the venue for the transaction, not a group consulted for advice.
